Headline: 20th Century Media Formats
Text: This is a sample timeline on twentieth-century media formats.

Headline: Phonograph cylinders
Text: Phonograph cylinders (also referred to as Edison cylinders after their creator Thomas Edison) are the earliest commercial medium for recording and reproducing sound.

Headline: Motion picture film
Text: Began as silent short films in nickelodes, evolving into synchronized sound ("talkies"), technicolor features, and educational film strips.
Media Caption: The oldest surviving motion picture film in the world is the Roundhay Garden Scene.

Headline: Cable television
Text: Cable television was invented in 1948 in the United States as Community Antenna Television (CATV). It originated independently in rural areas of Pennsylvania and Oregon.
Media Caption: A sign warning about a buried CATV cable in the area.

Headline: LP Record
Text: An LP (short for Long Play) is a 12-inch or 10-inch analog vinyl LP record that spins at 33⅓ RPM (revolutions per minute).

Headline: Cloud Storage
Text: Cloud storage is a model of computer data storage where digital files are saved on remote, internet-accessible servers managed by a third-party provider instead of a local hard drive or physical device.

Headline: Cassette Tape
Text: A cassette tape (Compact Cassette) is an analog magnetic tape recording format for audio playback and recording, housed in a small plastic shell.

Headline: CD
Text: Compact Discs (CDs) were made by using a focused laser beam to encode high-quality digital audio signals onto discs containing up to 82 minutes of sound storage.

Headline: MP3
Text: The Moving Picture Experts Group (MPEG) audio standard uses an algorithm to represent and share sound data electronically.
